l: Jesus's death and resurrection, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 17
s: Jesus tells the disciples not to speak of the vision until the Son of Man has risen from the dead. He says he will suffer at the hands of men, be delivered up and killed, and be raised on the third day, which grieves the disciples greatly.

l: The Gospel According to Matthew, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 18
s: In Matthew 18, the disciples ask Jesus who is greatest in the Kingdom of Heaven, and he sets a little child among them and says that humbling oneself like the child is the way to greatness. He warns against causing little ones who believe in him to stumble, urges drastic measures against sin, and tells of a shepherd seeking one lost sheep because the Father does not want any little one to perish. He then gives steps for dealing with a brother who sins: speak privately, take witnesses, tell the assembly, and treat the unrepentant one as a Gentile or tax collector, with sayings on binding, releasing, and gathering in his name. When Peter asks how often to forgive, Jesus answers seventy times seven and tells the parable of a king who forgave a servant ten thousand talents, only for that servant to imprison a fellow servant over one hundred denarii, and so be handed to the tormentors.

l: Jesus, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 18
s: Jesus answers the disciples' question about greatness by setting a little child among them and teaching humility. He warns about stumbling, tells the parable of the lost sheep, instructs on handling a sinning brother, and tells Peter to forgive until seventy times seven. He illustrates this with the parable of the king and the servants, and says he is present where two or three gather in his name.

l: Peter, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 18
s: Peter asks Jesus how often he should forgive his brother who sins against him, suggesting seven times. Jesus replies that it should be seventy times seven.

l: disciples, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 18
s: The disciples ask Jesus who is greatest in the Kingdom of Heaven. Jesus sets a child among them and tells them they must turn and become like little children to enter the Kingdom.

l: little child (set in the middle of the disciples), The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 18
s: Jesus calls the little child to himself and places the child in the middle of the disciples. The child serves as the example of humility: whoever humbles himself like this child is greatest in the Kingdom of Heaven, and whoever receives such a child in Jesus' name receives him.

l: little ones (who believe in Jesus), The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 18
s: Jesus warns that causing one of these little ones to stumble would deserve being sunk in the sea with a millstone. They are not to be despised, since their angels always see the face of the Father in heaven. It is not the Father's will that any of them perish.

l: Kingdom of Heaven, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 18
s: The disciples ask who is greatest in it, and Jesus says entry requires turning and becoming like little children, and greatness belongs to the one who humbles himself like a child. Jesus also likens it to a king settling accounts with his servants.

l: God, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 18
s: The Father's angels-in-attendance see his face in heaven, and it is not his will that any little one perish. He will answer agreement in prayer by two on earth, and Jesus says he will deal with those who do not forgive their brothers from the heart as the king dealt with the unforgiving servant.

l: occasions of stumbling, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 18
s: Jesus says woe comes to the world because of them and to the person through whom they come, though they must come. He teaches that a hand, foot, or eye that causes stumbling should be cut off or plucked out, since entering life maimed or with one eye is better than being cast into the Gehenna of fire.

l: brother who sins, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 18
s: If he sins against someone, that person should show him his fault privately, then with one or two witnesses, then before the assembly. If he refuses to hear even the assembly, he is to be treated as a Gentile or a tax collector, but if he listens, the brother is regained.

l: church discipline (binding and releasing), The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 18
s: Jesus says that whatever is bound on earth will have been bound in heaven, and whatever is released on earth will have been released in heaven. He adds that agreement of two on earth in prayer will be done by the Father, and that where two or three gather in his name he is among them.

l: forgiveness, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 18
s: Jesus tells Peter to forgive not seven times but seventy times seven. The parable of the king and servants shows that having been forgiven a great debt calls for mercy to others, and that the heavenly Father will deal severely with those who do not forgive their brothers from the heart.

l: king (in the parable), The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 18
s: The king settles accounts with his servants and, moved with compassion, forgives the servant who owed ten thousand talents and begged for patience. When told of that servant's treatment of his fellow servant, he calls him wicked, becomes angry, and delivers him to the tormentors until he pays all.

l: unforgiving servant, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 18
s: This servant owes the king ten thousand talents, begs for patience, and is released and forgiven. He then seizes a fellow servant who owes one hundred denarii, refuses his plea, and has him jailed, so the king calls him wicked and delivers him to the tormentors until he pays all that is due.

l: fellow servant (who owed one hundred denarii), The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 18
s: This servant owes the unforgiving servant one hundred denarii and is grabbed by the throat and told to pay. He falls down and begs for patience, but is cast into prison until he pays, and other servants, seeing this, report it to the lord.

l: The Gospel According to Matthew, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 19
s: Jesus leaves Galilee for Judea beyond the Jordan, where crowds follow and he heals them. Pharisees test him on divorce, and he answers by pointing to creation and the union of husband and wife, saying Moses allowed divorce only because of hardness of heart, and that divorce except for sexual immorality followed by remarriage is adultery. His disciples respond that marriage seems inadvisable, and he speaks of eunuchs and of those able to receive his saying. He then welcomes little children over the disciples' rebuke, and a young man with great possessions asks how to gain eternal life, but goes away sad when told to sell what he has and follow Jesus. Jesus teaches that it is hard for the rich to enter God's Kingdom, and when Peter asks what the disciples will receive, Jesus promises them thrones and a hundredfold reward to all who leave things for his name.

l: Jesus, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 19
s: Jesus departs from Galilee into Judea beyond the Jordan, heals the multitudes, and answers the Pharisees on divorce by appealing to creation and Moses's concession. He blesses the children, tells the young man to keep the commandments and then to sell his goods and follow him, and teaches that salvation is impossible for men but possible for God. He promises the disciples twelve thrones and a hundredfold reward, ending with 'many will be last who are first.'

l: Pharisees, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 19
s: The Pharisees come to Jesus to test him, asking whether it is lawful to divorce a wife for any reason. When Jesus answers from creation, they object by citing Moses's command to give a certificate of divorce.

l: disciples (Jesus's disciples), The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 19
s: The disciples react to Jesus's teaching on divorce by saying it is not expedient to marry, and they rebuke those bringing little children to him. They are exceedingly astonished at his saying about the rich and ask who can be saved. Jesus promises that they will sit on twelve thrones judging the twelve tribes of Israel.

l: Peter, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 19
s: Peter speaks up after the young man leaves, saying that the disciples have left everything to follow Jesus and asking what they will have. Jesus answers with a promise of reward in the regeneration.

l: rich young man (the one who came to Jesus), The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 19
s: The young man calls Jesus 'Good teacher' and asks what good thing he must do for eternal life. He says he has kept the commandments named by Jesus from his youth and asks what he still lacks. Told to sell his possessions, give to the poor, and follow Jesus, he goes away sad because he had great possessions.

l: God, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 19
s: Jesus says that God made people male and female from the beginning and joins husband and wife together, so man must not tear them apart. He says no one is good but God alone, and that all things are possible with God. The Kingdom of God is the one the rich enter only with difficulty.

l: divorce, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 19
s: The Pharisees ask whether divorce is lawful for any reason. Jesus says Moses allowed it because of hardness of hearts, but it was not so from the beginning. He states that whoever divorces his wife except for sexual immorality and marries another commits adultery, and so does the man who marries a divorced woman.

l: marriage, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 19
s: Jesus describes marriage as a man leaving his father and mother and being joined to his wife so that the two become one flesh, which God has joined and man must not separate. The disciples respond that if so, it is not expedient to marry. Jesus says not all can receive this saying, and he speaks of eunuchs, including those who make themselves so for the Kingdom of Heaven's sake.

l: Kingdom of Heaven, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 19
s: Jesus says the Kingdom of Heaven belongs to ones like little children. He says some make themselves eunuchs for its sake, and that a rich man enters it with difficulty, more easily a camel passing through a needle's eye. He also refers to it as God's Kingdom.

l: eternal life, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 19
s: The young man asks what good thing he must do to have eternal life, and Jesus tells him to enter life by keeping the commandments, then to sell his goods, give to the poor, and follow him. At the end Jesus says everyone who leaves family or lands for his name's sake will receive a hundredfold and inherit eternal life.

l: possessions and wealth, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 19
s: The young man's great possessions lead him to go away sad when Jesus tells him to sell them and give to the poor for treasure in heaven. Jesus says a rich man enters the Kingdom with difficulty, comparing it to a camel going through a needle's eye. He says those who leave houses, lands, and family for his name will receive a hundredfold.

l: The Gospel According to Matthew, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 20
s: Jesus tells a parable in which the master of a household hires laborers at various hours of the day for his vineyard and pays all of them a denarius, prompting the first-hired to murmur; he concludes that the last will be first and the first last. On the way up to Jerusalem, Jesus tells the twelve disciples that the Son of Man will be delivered, condemned, mocked, scourged, crucified, and raised on the third day. The mother of the sons of Zebedee asks that her two sons sit at his right and left in his Kingdom, and Jesus says they will drink his cup but that those seats are prepared by his Father. The other ten are indignant, and Jesus teaches that greatness among them comes through serving, as the Son of Man came to serve and give his life as a ransom for many. Leaving Jericho, Jesus stops for two blind men who cry out for mercy despite the crowd's rebuke, and he heals them with compassion.

l: Jesus, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 20
s: Jesus tells the vineyard parable, foretells his condemnation, crucifixion, and resurrection to the twelve, and answers the request for places in his Kingdom by saying they are not his to give but prepared by his Father. He teaches that greatness means servanthood, and he stops, asks the two blind men what they want, and heals them by touching their eyes out of compassion.

l: master of the household (parable), The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 20
s: The master goes out early in the morning and again at the third, sixth, ninth, and eleventh hours to hire laborers for his vineyard. At evening he has his manager pay everyone a denarius, last to first, and answers the complaining first laborers that he has done no wrong, may do what he wants with what he owns, and is good.

l: laborers (parable), The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 20
s: The laborers are hired at different hours, the first for a denarius agreed upon and the others for whatever is right. All receive a denarius, and those hired first murmur that the last, who worked one hour, were made equal to them. The master tells one of them to take what is his and go his way.

l: Kingdom of Heaven, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 20
s: The Kingdom of Heaven is likened to a master of a household hiring laborers for his vineyard, with the parable ending that the last will be first and the first last, and that many are called but few chosen. The mother of the sons of Zebedee asks for her sons to sit at Jesus's right and left in his Kingdom, and Jesus says those places are for whom his Father has prepared them.

l: Jesus's death and resurrection, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 20
s: On the way up to Jerusalem, Jesus takes the twelve aside and says the Son of Man will be delivered to the chief priests and scribes, who will condemn him to death. They will hand him over to the Gentiles to mock, scourge, and crucify him, and on the third day he will be raised up.

l: mother of the sons of Zebedee, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 20
s: She comes to Jesus with her sons, kneeling, and asks that they sit one on his right and one on his left in his Kingdom. Jesus replies that she does not know what she is asking.

l: sons of Zebedee, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 20
s: The two sons come with their mother, and Jesus asks if they can drink his cup and be baptized with his baptism; they say they are able. Jesus says they will indeed drink his cup, but the seats at his right and left are for those prepared by his Father, and the other ten are indignant with the two brothers.

l: two blind men, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 20
s: Sitting by the road near Jericho, the two blind men cry out to Jesus as Lord and son of David for mercy, and cry out all the more when the multitude rebukes them. Asked what they want, they request that their eyes be opened; Jesus touches their eyes, they immediately see, and they follow him.

l: The Gospel According to Matthew, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 21
s: Jesus approaches Jerusalem, sending two disciples to fetch a donkey and colt, and enters to crowds shouting 'Hosanna to the son of David!' He drives the sellers and money changers out of the temple, heals the lame and blind, and answers the indignant chief priests and scribes by citing Scripture about children's praise. He curses a fig tree that withers and teaches the disciples about faith and prayer. When the chief priests and elders challenge his authority, he counters with a question about John's baptism, then tells the parables of the two sons and the wicked farmers, which the chief priests and Pharisees perceive to be about them, though they fear the multitudes and do not seize him.

l: Jesus, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 21
s: Jesus enters Jerusalem on a donkey and colt, fulfilling the prophecy of the King who comes humbly. He drives out the temple sellers, heals the lame and blind, curses a fig tree, teaches about faith and prayer, and answers the challenge to his authority with a counter-question and two parables. The chief priests and Pharisees perceive the parables to be about them and seek to seize him but fear the multitudes.

l: Jerusalem, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 21
s: Jesus comes near Jerusalem and enters it, and the whole city is stirred up, asking 'Who is this?' The multitudes answer that he is the prophet, Jesus, from Nazareth of Galilee. Jesus goes out of the city to Bethany to camp and returns to it in the morning.

l: multitudes (crowds around Jesus), The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 21
s: A very great multitude spreads clothes and branches on the road, and those going in front and following shout 'Hosanna to the son of David!' They identify Jesus as the prophet from Nazareth of Galilee. The chief priests and Pharisees fear them and so do not seize Jesus, because the multitudes consider him a prophet.

l: temple, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 21
s: Jesus enters the temple of God and drives out those buying and selling, overturning the money changers' tables and the dove sellers' seats. He calls it a house of prayer that has been made a den of robbers. The lame and blind come to him there and are healed, children cry 'Hosanna' there, and he later teaches there when challenged by the chief priests and elders.

l: chief priests, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 21
s: The chief priests, with the scribes, are indignant at the wonders and at the children's praise in the temple. With the elders they ask by what authority Jesus acts, but they cannot answer his question about John's baptism, saying 'We don't know.' Hearing his parables, they perceive he speaks about them and seek to seize him but fear the multitudes.

l: fig tree, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 21
s: Jesus, hungry, finds nothing but leaves on a fig tree by the road. He tells it 'Let there be no fruit from you forever,' and it immediately withers. The disciples marvel, and Jesus uses it to teach about faith and prayer.

l: Jesus' authority, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 21
s: The chief priests and elders ask by what authority Jesus does these things and who gave it to him. Jesus answers with a question about whether John's baptism was from heaven or from men. Because they will not answer, he declines to tell them the source of his authority.

l: John the Baptizer, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 21
s: John's baptism is the subject of Jesus' counter-question, which traps the leaders since all hold John as a prophet. Jesus says John came in the way of righteousness; the tax collectors and prostitutes believed him, but the leaders did not, even after seeing this.

l: tax collectors and prostitutes, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 21
s: Jesus says the tax collectors and the prostitutes are entering God's Kingdom before the chief priests and elders. They believed John, whereas the leaders did not believe him and did not repent afterward.

l: parable of the two sons, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 21
s: Jesus tells of a man whose first son says he will not work in the vineyard but afterward changes his mind and goes, while the second says 'I'm going, sir' but does not go. The leaders answer that the first did the father's will. Jesus applies it to them: the tax collectors and prostitutes who believed John are like the first son.

l: parable of the wicked farmers, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 21
s: Jesus tells of a vineyard leased to farmers who beat, kill and stone the owner's servants and then kill his son. The leaders themselves say the owner will destroy those men and lease the vineyard to others. Jesus follows with the rejected stone saying, and the chief priests and Pharisees perceive that the parable is about them.

l: master of the household (vineyard owner), The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 21
s: The master plants a vineyard, sets a hedge, digs a wine press, builds a tower, leases it to farmers and goes to another country. He sends servants, then his son, to receive the fruit. The leaders say he will miserably destroy the farmers and lease the vineyard to others who will give fruit in season.

l: farmers (vineyard tenants), The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 21
s: The farmers beat one servant, kill another and stone another, and treat a second group of servants the same way. They kill the owner's son to seize his inheritance. The leaders judge that they will be miserably destroyed and replaced by other farmers.

l: son (vineyard master's son), The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 21
s: The master sends his son last, saying 'They will respect my son.' The farmers recognize him as the heir, throw him out of the vineyard and kill him. Jesus follows with the stone the builders rejected, which became the head of the corner.

l: God's Kingdom, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 21
s: Jesus says the tax collectors and prostitutes are entering God's Kingdom before the leaders. He also says it will be taken away from them and given to a nation producing its fruit.

l: temple cleansing, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 21
s: Jesus drives out all who sold and bought in the temple and overturns the money changers' tables and the dove sellers' seats. He cites 'My house shall be called a house of prayer' and accuses them of making it a den of robbers. Afterward he heals the lame and blind there, and the chief priests and scribes become indignant.

l: The Gospel According to Matthew, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 22
s: Jesus tells a parable of a king who gives a wedding feast for his son; the invited guests refuse and kill his servants, so the king destroys them and fills the feast with whomever the servants find, until he casts out a man without wedding clothing. The Pharisees and Herodians then try to trap Jesus over paying taxes to Caesar, and he answers that Caesar's things go to Caesar and God's things to God. The Sadducees pose a puzzle about a woman who married seven brothers in turn, and Jesus replies that in the resurrection people are like angels and that God is the God of the living. A lawyer among the Pharisees asks about the greatest commandment, and Jesus names love of God and love of neighbor. Jesus then asks the Pharisees how the Christ can be David's son if David calls him Lord, and no one can answer him or dare question him further.

l: Jesus, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 22
s: Jesus tells the parable of the wedding feast and then answers three tests in turn: the Pharisees' tax question, the Sadducees' resurrection puzzle, and a lawyer's question about the greatest commandment. He then asks the Pharisees how the Christ can be David's son and Lord, and no one can answer him or dares ask him more questions.

l: king (in the parable of the wedding feast), The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 22
s: The king makes a wedding feast for his son and sends servants to call the invited, who refuse. He destroys the murderers and burns their city, has others invited from the highways, and orders the man without wedding clothing bound and thrown into the outer darkness.

l: servants (the king's servants), The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 22
s: The servants are sent to call the invited guests, and some are seized, shamefully treated and killed. They are then sent to the highways and gather all they find, both bad and good, and later the king orders them to bind and remove the man without wedding clothing.

l: invited guests (of the wedding feast), The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 22
s: The invited guests refuse to come, make light of the invitation, and go to their farm or merchandise, while the rest kill the king's servants. The king declares them unworthy, destroys them and burns their city.

l: wedding feast (the king's son's), The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 22
s: The wedding feast is prepared with cattle and fatlings killed and everything ready. After the invited refuse, it is filled with guests gathered from the highways, both bad and good.

l: Kingdom of Heaven, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 22
s: Jesus says the Kingdom of Heaven is like a king who made a wedding feast for his son. The parable ends with the statement that many are called but few chosen.

l: man without wedding clothing, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 22
s: The king sees this man among the guests and asks how he came in without wedding clothing, and he is speechless. The king orders him bound hand and foot and thrown into the outer darkness, where there is weeping and grinding of teeth.

l: Pharisees, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 22
s: The Pharisees take counsel to entrap Jesus and send their disciples with the Herodians to ask about taxes to Caesar. They marvel at his answer, gather again after he silences the Sadducees, and send a lawyer to test him. Jesus then questions them about the Christ, and they say he is David's son but cannot answer further.

l: Caesar, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 22
s: Caesar's image and inscription are on the denarius shown to Jesus. Jesus says to give to Caesar the things that are Caesar's.

l: tax question, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 22
s: The Pharisees' disciples and the Herodians ask Jesus whether it is lawful to pay taxes to Caesar, hoping to entrap him. Jesus calls them hypocrites, has them identify the image on a denarius as Caesar's, and says to give Caesar what is Caesar's and God what is God's, and they marvel and leave.

l: God, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 22
s: Jesus says to give to God the things that are God's, and that the Sadducees do not know the power of God. He says that in the resurrection people are like God's angels, and that God, who called himself the God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, is the God of the living, not the dead.

l: Sadducees, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 22
s: The Sadducees, who say there is no resurrection, ask Jesus about a woman who married seven brothers in turn. Jesus tells them they are mistaken, not knowing the Scriptures or the power of God, and the Pharisees hear that he has silenced them.

l: resurrection, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 22
s: The Sadducees deny the resurrection and use a case of seven brothers to challenge it. Jesus says that in the resurrection people neither marry nor are given in marriage but are like God's angels, and that God is the God of the living.

l: seven brothers, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 22
s: In the Sadducees' hypothetical, the seven brothers each marry the same woman in turn after the previous brother dies without offspring. The Sadducees use this to ask whose wife she will be in the resurrection.

l: woman (wife of the seven brothers), The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 22
s: In the Sadducees' puzzle, she is married to the first brother, then to each of the others after each dies without offspring, and she dies last. The Sadducees ask whose wife she will be in the resurrection, and Jesus answers that people neither marry nor are given in marriage there.

l: lawyer (one of the Pharisees), The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 22
s: A lawyer among the Pharisees asks Jesus, testing him, which is the greatest commandment in the law. Jesus answers with love of God and love of neighbor.

l: greatest commandment, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 22
s: Jesus says the first and great commandment is to love the Lord your God with all your heart, soul and mind. The second is to love your neighbor as yourself, and the whole law and the prophets depend on these two.

l: Christ, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 22
s: Jesus asks the Pharisees whose son the Christ is, and they answer that he is David's son. Jesus points out that David in the Spirit calls him Lord and asks how he can then be David's son.

l: David, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 22
s: The Pharisees say the Christ is David's son. Jesus quotes David, speaking in the Spirit, as calling the Christ Lord, and asks how he can then be David's son.

l: The Gospel According to Matthew, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 23
s: Jesus speaks to the multitudes and his disciples about the scribes and the Pharisees, who sit on Moses' seat. He tells people to observe what they say but not to imitate their works, since they burden others, seek honor and titles, and do everything to be seen by men. He tells his followers not to take the titles Rabbi, father, or master, and says the greatest among them will be a servant. He then pronounces a series of woes on the scribes and Pharisees as hypocrites, condemning their shutting up the Kingdom of Heaven, their proselytizing, their oaths, their neglect of justice, mercy, and faith, and their outward cleanliness hiding inner corruption. He ends by lamenting over Jerusalem, which kills the prophets, and declares its house desolate until it says 'Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord!'

l: Jesus, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 23
s: Jesus addresses the multitudes and his disciples, instructing them to observe what the scribes and Pharisees teach but not their works, and teaching that one is Father, teacher, and master, and that the greatest is a servant. He pronounces woes on the scribes and Pharisees, calling them hypocrites, blind guides, serpents, and offspring of vipers, and says he will send prophets, wise men, and scribes to them. He laments over Jerusalem, wishing to gather her children like a hen gathers her chicks, and says they will not see him until they say 'Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord!'

l: scribes and the Pharisees, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 23
s: The scribes and Pharisees sit on Moses' seat, but they say and do not do, bind heavy burdens on others, and do their works to be seen by men. Jesus pronounces repeated woes on them as hypocrites for devouring widows' houses, shutting the Kingdom of Heaven against men, making proselytes twice as much sons of Gehenna, swearing falsely, neglecting justice, mercy, and faith, and being clean outside but full of extortion and iniquity within. He says they testify against themselves as children of those who killed the prophets, and that the blood of the righteous and judgment will come upon this generation.

l: Jerusalem, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 23
s: Jesus addresses Jerusalem as the city that kills the prophets and stones those sent to her. He says he often would have gathered her children as a hen gathers her chicks, but they would not. He declares that her house is left desolate and that she will not see him until she says 'Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord!'

l: hypocrisy and religious show, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 23
s: Jesus describes the scribes and Pharisees as acting to be seen by men: broad phylacteries, enlarged fringes, places of honor, salutations, and titles like 'Rabbi'. He compares them to cleaned cups and whitened tombs that look good outside but are full of extortion, uncleanness, hypocrisy, and iniquity within. He contrasts this with humility, saying whoever exalts himself will be humbled and whoever humbles himself will be exalted.

l: The Gospel According to Matthew, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 24
s: Jesus leaves the temple and tells his disciples that not one stone of its buildings will be left on another. On the Mount of Olives the disciples privately ask when this will happen and what the sign of his coming and of the end of the age will be. Jesus warns of false christs, wars, famines, and earthquakes as the beginning of birth pains, then describes persecution, the abomination of desolation, and a great suffering that will be shortened for the chosen ones. He says the Son of Man will come visibly on the clouds after those days, gathering the chosen, while no one but the Father knows the day or hour. He urges watchfulness through the days of Noah, the thief, and the faithful and evil servants.

l: Jesus, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 24
s: Jesus leaves the temple and predicts that its stones will all be thrown down. On the Mount of Olives he answers the disciples' private question by teaching about warnings, persecution, the great suffering, his coming as Son of Man, and the need to be watchful and ready. He says only the Father knows the day and hour.

l: disciples (Jesus's disciples), The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 24
s: The disciples point out the temple buildings to Jesus, then come to him privately on the Mount of Olives to ask when these things will be and what the sign of his coming and the end of the age is. They are warned not to be led astray, told they will be hated and delivered up, and urged to watch and be ready.

l: temple, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 24
s: The temple's buildings are shown to Jesus by his disciples. He says not one stone will be left on another that will not be thrown down. The abomination of desolation is also said to stand in the holy place.

l: false christs and false prophets, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 24
s: Many will come in Jesus's name claiming to be the Christ and will lead many astray. They will show great signs and wonders to deceive even the chosen ones if possible, and people are told not to believe claims that he is in the wilderness or the inner rooms.

l: end of the age, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 24
s: The disciples ask for its sign. Jesus says wars, rumors of wars, famines, plagues, and earthquakes are only the beginning of birth pains and that the end is not yet. The end will come after the Good News of the Kingdom is preached in the whole world as a testimony to all nations.

l: coming of the Son of Man, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 24
s: Jesus says it will be as visible as lightning flashing from east to west. After the suffering of those days, the sign of the Son of Man will appear, all the tribes of the earth will mourn, and he will come on the clouds with power and great glory, sending angels to gather the chosen. Its day and hour are known only to the Father, and it will come unexpectedly, as in the days of Noah.

l: tribulation, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 24
s: Jesus describes a time of great suffering, unmatched from the beginning of the world, that follows the abomination of desolation, when those in Judea must flee. Those days will be shortened for the sake of the chosen ones, since otherwise no flesh would be saved. Immediately after it, the sun and moon will darken and the stars will fall.

l: servant (faithful and wise), The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 24
s: Jesus describes this servant as one whom his lord sets over his household to give food in due season. If the lord finds him doing so on arrival, he is blessed and will be set over all that the lord has.

l: evil servant, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 24
s: This servant says in his heart that his lord is delaying, then beats his fellow servants and eats and drinks with drunkards. His lord will come unexpectedly, cut him in pieces, and appoint his portion with the hypocrites, where there will be weeping and grinding of teeth.

l: The Gospel According to Matthew, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 25
s: Chapter 25 presents three teachings about the Kingdom of Heaven and the coming of the Son of Man. In the first, ten virgins await a bridegroom; the five wise ones bring oil and enter the wedding feast, while the five foolish ones lack oil, go to buy it, and are shut out. In the second, a man going into another country entrusts five, two, and one talent to his servants; the first two double their talents and are praised, while the servant who buried his one talent is condemned and cast into the outer darkness. In the third, the Son of Man, as King, gathers all the nations and separates sheep from goats, welcoming the righteous who served the least of his brothers into eternal life and sending those who did not into eternal punishment. The chapter repeatedly stresses watchfulness, readiness, and faithful action.

l: Kingdom of Heaven, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 25
s: The Kingdom of Heaven is likened to ten virgins who took their lamps and went out to meet the bridegroom. The parable shows that some are ready and are admitted, while others are not.

l: ten virgins, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 25
s: The ten virgins took their lamps and went out to meet the bridegroom, and all slumbered and slept while he delayed. At midnight a cry announced his coming and all arose and trimmed their lamps, but only five were ready to go in.

l: bridegroom, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 25
s: The bridegroom delayed, then came at midnight after a cry announced him. He took those who were ready into the wedding feast, the door was shut, and he told the late virgins who cried 'Lord, Lord' that he did not know them.

l: Son of Man, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 25
s: The Son of Man is said to be coming at a day and hour no one knows, so people are told to watch. He will come in his glory with all the holy angels and sit on the throne of his glory.

l: servant with five talents, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 25
s: The servant with five talents immediately traded with them and gained another five. His lord called him a good and faithful servant, promised to set him over many things, and invited him to enter the joy of his lord.

l: servant with two talents, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 25
s: The servant with two talents gained another two in the same way. His lord gave him the same praise and promise as the first servant: faithful over a few things, set over many, and welcomed into the joy of his lord.

l: servant with one talent, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 25
s: The servant with one talent dug in the earth and hid his lord's money, explaining that he knew his lord was a hard man and was afraid. His lord called him wicked and slothful, said he should have deposited the money with bankers for interest, took the talent from him, and had him thrown into the outer darkness.

l: nations, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 25
s: All the nations will be gathered before the Son of Man on his throne. He will separate them one from another as a shepherd separates sheep from goats.

l: sheep, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 25
s: The sheep are set on the King's right hand and called blessed of his Father. They inherit the Kingdom prepared from the foundation of the world because they fed, gave drink to, took in, clothed, and visited him in the least of these.

l: goats, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 25
s: The goats are set on the King's left hand and told to depart, cursed, into the eternal fire prepared for the devil and his angels. They are condemned because they did not feed, give drink to, take in, clothe, or visit him, and they go away into eternal punishment.

l: righteous, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 25
s: The righteous ask when they saw the King hungry, thirsty, a stranger, naked, sick, or in prison and helped him. They are told that serving the least of his brothers was serving him, and they go into eternal life.

l: The Gospel According to Matthew, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 26
s: In Matthew 26, Jesus tells his disciples that the Passover is two days away and that he will be delivered up to be crucified, while the chief priests, scribes, and elders plot with Caiaphas to seize him by deceit. A woman anoints Jesus in Bethany, and Judas Iscariot agrees to betray him for thirty pieces of silver. At the Passover meal Jesus predicts his betrayal and denial by Peter, gives the bread and cup as his body and blood of the new covenant, and then prays in Gethsemane while the disciples sleep. Judas leads a crowd to arrest Jesus with a kiss, the disciples flee, and the council tries Jesus before Caiaphas, declaring him worthy of death for blasphemy after he affirms he is the Son of Man who will sit at the right hand of Power. Meanwhile Peter follows at a distance, denies Jesus three times, hears the rooster crow, and weeps bitterly.

l: Jesus, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 26
s: Jesus foretells his crucifixion, defends the woman who anoints him as preparing him for burial, and keeps the Passover with the twelve, predicting his betrayal and Peter's denial. He prays in anguish at Gethsemane, submits to the Father's will, is arrested, rebukes the sword-wielding follower, and before the council says he is the Son of Man who will sit at the right hand of Power. He is spat on, beaten, and declared worthy of death.

l: twelve disciples, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 26
s: The disciples protest the anointing as waste, prepare the Passover as Jesus commands, and each asks whether he is the betrayer. They sleep while Jesus prays in Gethsemane, and all leave him and flee when he is arrested, despite their claims they would not stumble.

l: Judas Iscariot, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 26
s: Judas, one of the twelve, goes to the chief priests and receives thirty pieces of silver to deliver Jesus. At the meal he asks 'It isn't me, is it, Rabbi?' and is told 'You said it.' He later leads the armed crowd and identifies Jesus with a kiss.

l: Peter, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 26
s: Peter vows never to stumble and to die with Jesus rather than deny him, and is among those taken to Gethsemane, where he is found sleeping. One follower draws a sword and cuts off the high priest's servant's ear at the arrest. Peter follows Jesus at a distance to the high priest's court, denies him three times, and weeps bitterly after the rooster crows.

l: chief priests, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 26
s: The chief priests, with the scribes and elders, gather in Caiaphas's court and plan to seize Jesus by deceit but not during the feast. They pay Judas thirty pieces of silver and send a crowd with swords and clubs to arrest Jesus. They seek false testimony against him at the trial.

l: Caiaphas, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 26
s: Caiaphas is the high priest in whose court the chief priests, scribes, and elders plot against Jesus. Jesus is led to him for trial, and he adjures Jesus to say whether he is the Christ, the Son of God. He tears his clothing and declares Jesus's answer blasphemy.

l: Passover, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 26
s: Jesus says the Passover is two days away and that he will be delivered up to be crucified then. On the first day of unleavened bread the disciples prepare the Passover at a certain person's house in the city, where Jesus eats it with the twelve.

l: Last Supper (Passover meal), The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 26
s: While reclining with the twelve, Jesus says one of them will betray him, identifying him as the one who dipped his hand in the dish, and tells Judas 'You said it.' He gives bread as his body and the cup as his blood of the new covenant poured out for many for remission of sins, and says he will not drink the fruit of the vine until he drinks it anew in his Father's Kingdom. They sing a hymn and go to the Mount of Olives.

l: Gethsemane, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 26
s: Jesus brings the disciples to Gethsemane, taking Peter and the two sons of Zebedee further with him, and says his soul is exceedingly sorrowful to death. He prays three times that the cup pass unless it is the Father's will, finding the disciples asleep each time. Judas and the crowd arrive there while he is still speaking.

l: betrayal and arrest of Jesus, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 26
s: Judas arrives with a great multitude with swords and clubs from the chief priests and elders and gives the sign of a kiss, greeting Jesus as Rabbi. Jesus calls him friend, is seized, and rebukes the follower who cuts off the servant's ear, saying he could ask the Father for more than twelve legions of angels and that this fulfills the Scriptures. All the disciples then leave him and flee.

l: trial before the council, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 26
s: At Caiaphas's house the chief priests, elders, and council seek false testimony; two witnesses finally claim Jesus said he could destroy the temple and rebuild it in three days. Jesus is silent until adjured by the high priest, then answers 'You have said so' and speaks of the Son of Man sitting at the right hand of Power. The council declares him worthy of death, and some spit on him, beat him, and slap him.

l: Peter's denial, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 26
s: While Jesus is tried, Peter sits in the court and is identified as a companion of Jesus by a maid, another person, and bystanders. He denies it three times, the last with cursing and swearing, saying 'I don't know the man.' The rooster crows, he remembers Jesus's prediction, and he goes out and weeps bitterly.

l: The Gospel According to Matthew, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 27
s: The chief priests and elders deliver Jesus to Pontius Pilate, the governor, and Judas, seeing Jesus condemned, returns the thirty pieces of silver, says he betrayed innocent blood, and hangs himself; the priests use the money to buy the potter's field. Pilate questions Jesus, who answers little, and offers the crowd a choice between Barabbas and Jesus; persuaded by the chief priests and elders, the multitude demands Barabbas and the crucifixion of Jesus, and Pilate washes his hands and has Jesus flogged and handed over. Soldiers mock Jesus, Simon of Cyrene is compelled to carry his cross, and Jesus is crucified at Golgotha between two robbers while passersby, priests, and the robbers mock him. Darkness falls, Jesus cries out and yields up his spirit, the temple veil tears, the earth quakes, tombs open, and the centurion says he was the Son of God. Joseph of Arimathaea, a disciple, obtains the body from Pilate and lays it in his new tomb, and the chief priests and Pharisees get Pilate's permission to secure the tomb with a guard and a sealed stone.

l: Jesus, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 27
s: Jesus is bound and delivered to Pilate, answers 'So you say' when asked if he is King of the Jews, and says nothing to the accusations. He is flogged, mocked by soldiers, crucified at Golgotha, cries 'My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?' and yields up his spirit. His body is buried in a new tomb.

l: Pontius Pilate, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 27
s: Pilate, the governor, questions Jesus and marvels at his silence, knowing the leaders delivered him up out of envy. After his wife's warning and the crowd's insistence, he washes his hands, declares himself innocent of the blood of this righteous person, releases Barabbas, and has Jesus flogged and handed over to be crucified. He later gives Jesus' body to Joseph and tells the priests and Pharisees to secure the tomb with a guard.

l: Judas Iscariot, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 27
s: Judas, who betrayed Jesus, feels remorse on seeing him condemned and returns the thirty pieces of silver, saying he sinned by betraying innocent blood. The chief priests refuse responsibility, and he throws the silver down in the sanctuary and hangs himself.

l: chief priests, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 27
s: The chief priests and elders take counsel to put Jesus to death, bind him, and deliver him to Pilate. They rebuff Judas, use the returned silver to buy the potter's field, persuade the crowd to ask for Barabbas, and mock Jesus on the cross. Afterward they ask Pilate to secure the tomb and seal the stone with a guard.

l: Barabbas, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 27
s: Barabbas is described as a notable prisoner. The crowd chooses him over Jesus, and Pilate releases him.

l: multitude, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 27
s: The multitude, persuaded by the chief priests and elders, asks for Barabbas and repeatedly cries 'Let him be crucified!' When Pilate washes his hands, all the people answer, 'May his blood be on us and on our children!'

l: crucifixion of Jesus, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 27
s: After being flogged and mocked, Jesus is led out, Simon of Cyrene is compelled to carry the cross, and Jesus is crucified at Golgotha with two robbers, his clothing divided by lot and an accusation reading 'THIS IS JESUS, THE KING OF THE JEWS' above him. Passersby, priests, and the robbers mock him; darkness covers the land from the sixth to the ninth hour, and he dies, followed by the torn veil, an earthquake, opened tombs, and the centurion's declaration.

l: Joseph of Arimathaea, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 27
s: Joseph, a rich man from Arimathaea and a disciple of Jesus, asks Pilate for Jesus' body and receives it. He wraps it in clean linen, lays it in his own new rock-cut tomb, and rolls a large stone against the door.

l: tomb, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 27
s: Joseph's new tomb, cut out in the rock, receives Jesus' body and is closed with a large stone while Mary Magdalene and the other Mary sit opposite. The next day the chief priests and Pharisees, recalling Jesus' saying about rising after three days, have it secured with a guard and a sealed stone at Pilate's permission.

l: The Gospel According to Matthew, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 28
s: At dawn on the first day of the week, Mary Magdalene and the other Mary come to the tomb, where an earthquake occurs and an angel of the Lord rolls away the stone, leaving the guards like dead men. The angel tells the women that Jesus has risen and instructs them to tell his disciples to go to Galilee, and Jesus himself meets the women and repeats the instruction. Some guards report to the chief priests, who, with the elders, pay the soldiers silver to say the disciples stole the body, a story that spreads among the Jews. The eleven disciples go to a mountain in Galilee, where they worship Jesus though some doubt, and Jesus declares all authority is his and commissions them to make disciples of all nations, baptize, and teach, promising to be with them always.

l: Jesus, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 28
s: Jesus is announced by the angel as risen from the dead, just as he said. He meets the women, greets them with "Rejoice!", accepts their worship, and tells them to have his brothers go to Galilee. In Galilee he tells the eleven that all authority in heaven and on earth has been given to him, commands them to make disciples of all nations, and promises to be with them always to the end of the age.

l: Mary Magdalene, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 28
s: Mary Magdalene comes with the other Mary at dawn to see the tomb. She hears the angel's message, runs with fear and great joy to tell the disciples, meets Jesus, takes hold of his feet, and worships him.

l: Mary the mother of James and Joses, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 28
s: The other Mary goes with Mary Magdalene to see the tomb at dawn on the first day of the week. She hears the angel announce the resurrection, hurries to tell the disciples, and takes hold of Jesus' feet and worships him when he meets her.

l: women (Mary Magdalene and the other Mary), The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 28
s: The women come to see the tomb and are told by the angel not to be afraid, that Jesus has risen, and to tell his disciples to go to Galilee. They leave quickly with fear and great joy, meet Jesus on the way, worship him, and receive his instruction to tell his brothers to go to Galilee.

l: angel (angel of the Lord), The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 28
s: An angel of the Lord descends from the sky amid a great earthquake, rolls away the stone from the tomb, and sits on it, with an appearance like lightning and clothing white as snow. He tells the women not to be afraid, shows them where Jesus lay, announces that Jesus has risen, and instructs them to tell the disciples that Jesus goes before them into Galilee.

l: tomb (Jesus' tomb), The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 28
s: The tomb is visited by the women at dawn on the first day of the week. Its stone is rolled away by the angel, who sits on it, and the women are shown the place where Jesus had lain, which is empty because he has risen.

l: guards (at Jesus' tomb), The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 28
s: The guards shake with fear of the angel and become like dead men. Some go into the city and report all that happened to the chief priests, then accept a large amount of silver and spread the story that the disciples stole the body while they slept.

l: chief priests, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 28
s: The chief priests hear the guards' report of what happened. They assemble with the elders, take counsel, and give a large amount of silver to the soldiers, telling them to say the disciples stole the body at night, and promising to persuade the governor and keep the soldiers free of worry.

l: disciples (Jesus's disciples), The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 28
s: The eleven disciples are told through the women to go to Galilee, and they go to the mountain where Jesus had sent them. There they bow down to Jesus, though some doubt, and receive his commission to make disciples of all nations, baptize them, and teach them to observe all he commanded.

l: Galilee, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 28
s: Galilee is named by the angel and by Jesus as the place where the disciples will see him. The eleven go there to a mountain where Jesus had sent them and meet him, and he gives them their commission.

l: resurrection of Jesus, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 28
s: The angel declares that Jesus has risen from the dead just as he said, and the empty tomb is shown to the women. Jesus then appears to the women and later to the eleven disciples in Galilee, who worship him though some doubt.

l: story of the stolen body, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 28
s: The chief priests and elders pay the soldiers to say that Jesus' disciples came by night and stole him away while the guards slept. The soldiers take the money and comply, and the saying spreads among the Jews and continues until the time of writing.

l: Great Commission, The Gospel According to Matthew, Chapter 28
s: On the mountain in Galilee, Jesus commands the eleven to go and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit, and teaching them to observe everything he commanded. He grounds this in his authority in heaven and on earth and promises to be with them always, even to the end of the age.

l: The Good News According to Mark, The Good News According to Mark, The Good News According to Mark / Chapter 1
s: Mark chapter 1 opens the Good News of Jesus Christ, the Son of God, citing the prophets' promise of a messenger. John baptizes in the Jordan with a baptism of repentance, draws crowds from Judea and Jerusalem, and announces a mightier one coming. Jesus is baptized by John, is declared the beloved Son by a voice from the sky, and is driven by the Spirit into the wilderness for forty days of temptation by Satan. After John is taken into custody, Jesus preaches God's Kingdom in Galilee, calls Simon, Andrew, James and John to follow him, and in Capernaum teaches with authority, casts out an unclean spirit, heals Simon's wife's mother and many others, and cleanses a leper, whose spreading of the news keeps Jesus in deserted places.

l: Jesus, The Good News According to Mark, The Good News According to Mark / Chapter 1
s: Jesus comes from Nazareth of Galilee, is baptized by John, is called beloved Son by a voice from the sky, and is tempted forty days in the wilderness. He then preaches God's Kingdom in Galilee, calls four fishermen, teaches with authority, casts out an unclean spirit, heals Simon's wife's mother, many sick and a leper, and prays in a deserted place, saying he came out to preach in other towns.

l: John, The Good News According to Mark, The Good News According to Mark / Chapter 1
s: John is clothed in camel's hair with a leather belt, eats locusts and wild honey, and baptizes in the Jordan while preaching repentance. He announces that one mightier than he is coming who will baptize in the Holy Spirit, baptizes Jesus, and is later taken into custody. A separate John, brother of James and son of Zebedee, is called by Jesus while mending nets and follows him.

l: Peter, The Good News According to Mark, The Good News According to Mark / Chapter 1
s: Simon is a fisherman casting a net with his brother Andrew when Jesus calls him to become a fisher for men, and he immediately leaves his nets and follows. Jesus then enters his house, where Simon's wife's mother is healed of a fever, and later Simon and those with him search for Jesus and tell him everyone is looking for him.

l: God, The Good News According to Mark, The Good News According to Mark / Chapter 1
s: God is the one whose Son is Jesus Christ; a voice from the sky says Jesus is the beloved Son in whom he is well pleased. Jesus preaches the Good News of God's Kingdom, which is said to be at hand, and the unclean spirit calls Jesus the Holy One of God.

l: baptism of repentance, The Good News According to Mark, The Good News According to Mark / Chapter 1
s: John preaches and carries out the baptism of repentance for forgiveness of sins in the Jordan river. People from all Judea and Jerusalem go out to him, are baptized, and confess their sins. John contrasts it with the coming baptism in the Holy Spirit.

l: Good News, The Good News According to Mark, The Good News According to Mark / Chapter 1
s: The Good News is introduced as that of Jesus Christ, the Son of God. Jesus preaches the Good News of God's Kingdom in Galilee, saying the time is fulfilled, and calls people to repent and believe in it.

l: man with an unclean spirit, The Good News According to Mark, The Good News According to Mark / Chapter 1
s: In the synagogue at Capernaum, the man with an unclean spirit cries out, asking what Jesus has to do with them and whether he has come to destroy them, and identifies Jesus as the Holy One of God. Jesus rebukes the spirit, which convulses the man, cries out loudly and comes out of him, amazing the onlookers.

l: leper, The Good News According to Mark, The Good News According to Mark / Chapter 1
s: A leper comes to Jesus, kneels, and begs to be made clean if Jesus is willing. Jesus, moved with compassion, touches him and says he wants to, and the leprosy leaves immediately. Told to say nothing and to show himself to the priest, the man instead spreads the news widely, so Jesus can no longer openly enter a city.

l: The Good News According to Mark, The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 2
s: Jesus returns to Capernaum, where a crowd gathers at his house and four people lower a paralytic through the roof to him. Jesus forgives the man's sins, answers the scribes' charge of blasphemy, and heals him so that he walks out, leaving everyone amazed. Jesus then calls Levi, the son of Alphaeus, from the tax office and eats at his house with many tax collectors and sinners, which draws criticism from the scribes and Pharisees. When asked why his disciples do not fast, Jesus answers with images of the bridegroom, unshrunk cloth, and new wine in old wineskins. Finally, the Pharisees object that his disciples pluck grain on the Sabbath, and Jesus cites David and declares that the Son of Man is lord even of the Sabbath.

l: Jesus, The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 2
s: Jesus returns to Capernaum, teaches the crowd, forgives and heals a paralytic, and perceives the scribes' hidden reasoning. He calls Levi, eats with tax collectors and sinners, says he came to call sinners to repentance, and defends his disciples on fasting and the Sabbath. He claims authority on earth to forgive sins and calls the Son of Man lord even of the Sabbath.

l: paralytic, The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 2
s: The paralytic is carried to Jesus and let down through the roof on a mat. Jesus tells him his sins are forgiven, then tells him to arise, take up his mat and go home, and he does so in front of everyone.

l: four people (who carried the paralytic), The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 2
s: Four people carry the paralytic to Jesus. Unable to get near him because of the crowd, they remove and break up the roof and lower the mat, and Jesus sees their faith.

l: scribes, The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 2
s: Some scribes sitting there reason in their hearts that Jesus blasphemes by forgiving sins, since only God can do so. Jesus perceives this and challenges them. Later, scribes of the Pharisees' party ask his disciples why he eats with tax collectors and sinners.

l: Pharisees, The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 2
s: The Pharisees, with the scribes, question why Jesus eats with tax collectors and sinners. Their disciples fast, and they ask why Jesus' disciples do not. They also object that his disciples pluck grain on the Sabbath, and Jesus answers by citing David.

l: Levi, The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 2
s: Levi, the son of Alphaeus, is sitting at the tax office when Jesus passes and says "Follow me." He arises and follows him.

l: tax collectors and sinners, The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 2
s: Many tax collectors and sinners sit down with Jesus and his disciples at the table in the house, and they follow him. Jesus says he came to call sinners to repentance, not the righteous.

l: disciples (Jesus's disciples), The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 2
s: Jesus' disciples are at the table with the tax collectors and sinners and are questioned about it by the scribes and Pharisees. They are not fasting, which Jesus explains while the bridegroom is with them. They pluck ears of grain on the Sabbath, and Jesus defends them.

l: fasting, The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 2
s: John's disciples and the Pharisees fast, while Jesus' disciples do not. Jesus says they cannot fast while the bridegroom is with them, but will fast in the days when he is taken away. He adds the sayings about unshrunk cloth on an old garment and new wine in old wineskins.

l: forgiveness of sins, The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 2
s: Jesus tells the paralytic his sins are forgiven, and the scribes consider this blasphemy because only God can forgive sins. Jesus says he heals the man so they may know the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins.

l: Sabbath, The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 2
s: The Pharisees say Jesus' disciples do what is not lawful on the Sabbath by plucking grain. Jesus cites David eating the show bread and says the Sabbath was made for man, not man for the Sabbath, and that the Son of Man is lord even of the Sabbath.

l: The Good News According to Mark, The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 3
s: In a synagogue, Jesus heals a man with a withered hand on the Sabbath while the Pharisees watch to accuse him, and they then conspire with the Herodians to destroy him. Jesus withdraws to the sea, where a great multitude from many regions follows him, and unclean spirits declare him the Son of God before he warns them to be silent. He goes up the mountain and appoints twelve, naming them, to be with him, preach, and have authority over sicknesses and demons. When his friends think he is insane and scribes from Jerusalem say he has Beelzebul, Jesus answers in parables about a divided Satan and a bound strong man, and warns of the unforgivable blasphemy against the Holy Spirit. His mother and brothers arrive outside, and he declares that whoever does the will of God is his brother, sister, and mother.

l: Jesus, The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 3
s: Jesus heals a man's withered hand in the synagogue on the Sabbath after asking whether it is lawful to do good or harm, and he is grieved at the hardness of his opponents' hearts. He draws a great multitude, is named Son of God by unclean spirits whom he sternly silences, and appoints twelve to be with him, preach, and cast out demons. Accused of having Beelzebul and thought insane by his friends, he answers with parables and redefines his family as those who do God's will.

l: man with withered hand (synagogue), The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 3
s: He is present in the synagogue with a withered hand and is told by Jesus to stand up and then to stretch out his hand. He stretches it out and it is restored as healthy as the other.

l: Sabbath, The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 3
s: The Sabbath is the day on which the Pharisees watch to see whether Jesus will heal, in order to accuse him. Jesus frames the question as whether it is lawful on the Sabbath to do good or harm, to save a life or kill, and his opponents are silent.

l: Pharisees, The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 3
s: The Pharisees watch Jesus in the synagogue to see if he will heal on the Sabbath so they can accuse him. After he heals the man, they go out and immediately conspire with the Herodians about how to destroy him.

l: multitude (following Jesus), The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 3
s: A great multitude follows Jesus from Galilee, Judea, Jerusalem, Idumaea, beyond the Jordan, and around Tyre and Sidon after hearing of what he did. Those with diseases press on him to touch him, so he asks for a little boat to stay near him, and the crowds later gather so tightly that he and his followers cannot eat. A multitude sits around him when his family comes.

l: the twelve apostles, The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 3
s: Jesus appoints twelve on the mountain so that they might be with him, be sent out to preach, and have authority to heal sicknesses and cast out demons. They are named as Simon (given the name Peter), James and John (called Boanerges, Sons of Thunder), Andrew, Philip, Bartholomew, Matthew, Thomas, James son of Alphaeus, Thaddaeus, Simon the Zealot, and Judas Iscariot, who also betrayed him.

l: scribes from Jerusalem, The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 3
s: The scribes who came down from Jerusalem say Jesus has Beelzebul and casts out demons by the prince of the demons. Jesus summons them and answers in parables that a divided kingdom, house, or Satan cannot stand.

l: Satan, The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 3
s: Jesus argues that Satan cannot cast out Satan, since a kingdom or house divided against itself cannot stand and Satan, if divided, would come to an end. He also likens Satan to a strong man whose house can be plundered only after he is bound.

l: Holy Spirit, The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 3
s: Jesus says that whoever blasphemes against the Holy Spirit never has forgiveness and is subject to eternal condemnation. The text explains he said this because they claimed he has an unclean spirit.

l: blasphemy, The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 3
s: Jesus says all sins and blasphemies of the descendants of man will be forgiven. The exception is blasphemy against the Holy Spirit, which never has forgiveness and brings eternal condemnation.

l: Jesus's mother, The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 3
s: Jesus's mother comes with his brothers and, standing outside, sends word calling him. Jesus responds by asking who his mother and brothers are and says that whoever does God's will is his mother, brother, and sister.

l: Jesus's brothers and sisters, The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 3
s: Jesus's brothers come with his mother and stand outside calling for him, and the crowd tells him his brothers and sisters are outside looking for him. Jesus answers by naming those sitting around him as his mother and brothers, and says whoever does the will of God is his brother and sister.

l: The Good News According to Mark, The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 4
s: In Chapter 4, Jesus teaches a large multitude by the seaside from a boat, telling the parable of the farmer who sows seed on four kinds of ground. Alone with those around him and the twelve, he explains that the seed is the word and that the soils represent different responses to it, and he says the mystery of God's Kingdom is given to them while outsiders receive parables. He adds sayings about a lamp, the measure given, and two Kingdom parables, the seed growing by itself and the mustard seed. That evening he crosses the sea with his disciples, sleeps in the boat during a wind storm, calms the wind and sea with a command, and asks why they are afraid and have no faith. The disciples are greatly afraid and ask who he is that the wind and sea obey him.

l: Jesus, The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 4
s: Jesus teaches the multitude by the sea from a boat, speaking in parables and privately explaining everything to his own disciples. He interprets the parable of the sower, says the mystery of God's Kingdom is given to those around him, and urges them to take heed what they hear. When a wind storm fills the boat, he wakes, rebukes the wind, says to the sea "Peace! Be still!", and brings a great calm, then asks the disciples why they are afraid and lack faith.

l: farmer (parable of the sower), The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 4
s: The farmer goes out to sow seed that falls on the road, rocky ground, thorns, and good ground. Jesus explains that the farmer sows the word.

l: seed (the sower's seed), The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 4
s: The seed is eaten by birds on the road, scorched on rocky ground for lack of root, and choked among thorns. On good ground it yields thirty, sixty, or one hundred times as much. Jesus identifies the seed with the word sown in people, and in other parables the Kingdom is likened to seed that grows by itself and to a tiny mustard seed that becomes greater than all herbs.

l: multitude (gathered to Jesus), The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 4
s: A great multitude gathers to Jesus by the sea, standing on the land while he teaches from the boat. He speaks the word to them in many parables, as they are able to hear it, and then leaves them behind when he and his disciples cross the sea.

l: disciples (those around him with the twelve), The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 4
s: Those around Jesus with the twelve ask him privately about the parables and are told that the mystery of God's Kingdom is given to them. Jesus asks whether they understand the parable of the sower and explains everything to them. In the storm they wake him, asking if he cares that they are dying, and after he calms it they are greatly afraid and ask who he is that the wind and sea obey him.

l: parables, The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 4
s: Jesus teaches the multitude many things in parables, and speaks to them only in parables, as they are able to hear. He tells the disciples that to those outside all things are done in parables, so that seeing they do not perceive, and he explains everything privately to his own disciples. He says that understanding the sower parable is needed to understand all the parables.

l: God's Kingdom, The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 4
s: Jesus says its mystery is given to the disciples but not to outsiders. He compares it to a man who casts seed and sleeps while the earth bears fruit by itself until harvest, and to a mustard seed, the smallest of seeds, that grows into a great plant where birds of the sky can lodge.

l: the word (of God), The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 4
s: The word is what the farmer sows. Satan takes it from those by the road, those on rocky ground receive it with joy but stumble under oppression or persecution, and the cares of the age, riches, and lusts choke it among thorns. Those on good ground hear it, accept it, and bear fruit thirty, sixty, or one hundred times.

l: sea, The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 4
s: The sea is the setting where Jesus teaches the multitude from a boat while they stand on the shore. During the evening crossing, Jesus commands it, "Peace! Be still!", and it becomes calm, so that the disciples marvel that it obeys him.

l: boat (Jesus's boat), The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 4
s: Jesus enters a boat and sits in it to teach the multitude on the shore. That evening the disciples take him across the sea in it, with other small boats accompanying. A storm fills the boat with waves while he sleeps on the cushion in the stern.

l: wind storm, The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 4
s: A big wind storm arises while Jesus and his disciples cross the sea, and waves beat into the boat until it is nearly filled. Jesus rebukes the wind, it ceases, and a great calm follows.

l: The Good News According to Mark, The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 5
s: Jesus crosses the sea to the country of the Gadarenes, where he frees a man living in the tombs from an unclean spirit named Legion, sending the demons into a herd of about two thousand pigs that drown in the sea. The townspeople, afraid, beg Jesus to leave, while the healed man is told to go home and proclaim what the Lord has done, which he does in Decapolis. Back across the sea, Jairus, a synagogue ruler, begs Jesus to heal his dying little daughter. On the way, a woman with a twelve-year flow of blood touches Jesus' clothes and is healed, and Jesus tells her that her faith has made her well. News comes that Jairus's daughter has died, but Jesus tells Jairus to believe, enters with Peter, James, John and the parents, and raises the twelve-year-old girl, ordering that she be given something to eat.

l: Jesus, The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 5
s: Jesus crosses to the country of the Gadarenes, commands the unclean spirit out of a man, and gives the demons permission to enter the pigs. He is asked by the people to leave, then returns across the sea, heals a woman who touches his clothes, and raises Jairus's daughter, taking only Peter, James, and John with him and strictly ordering that no one should know.

l: man with an unclean spirit (Gadarenes tombs), The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 5
s: He lives in the tombs, cannot be bound even with chains, and cries out night and day while cutting himself with stones. He runs to Jesus and bows down, is freed of the unclean spirit, and is then found sitting, clothed, and in his right mind. He begs to go with Jesus but is told to go home and tell what the Lord has done, and he proclaims it in Decapolis, where everyone marvels.

l: Legion, The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 5
s: Legion is the name the unclean spirit gives when Jesus asks, explaining that 'we are many.' The demons beg not to be sent out of the country and ask to be sent into the pigs, and Jesus permits it.

l: pigs (herd near Gadarenes), The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 5
s: A great herd of pigs, about two thousand, is feeding on the mountainside. The unclean spirits enter them at Jesus' permission, and the herd rushes down the steep bank into the sea and drowns.

l: Jairus, The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 5
s: Jairus, one of the rulers of the synagogue, falls at Jesus' feet and begs him to come lay hands on his little daughter, who is at the point of death. When word comes that she is dead, Jesus tells him not to be afraid but only to believe, and Jairus and his wife see the girl raised.

l: Jairus's daughter, The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 5
s: She is Jairus's little daughter, twelve years old, at the point of death and then reported dead. Jesus says she is asleep, takes her by the hand and says 'Talitha cumi,' and she immediately rises and walks. Jesus orders that she be given something to eat.

l: woman with discharge of blood, The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 5
s: She has had a discharge of blood for twelve years, has suffered under many physicians, spent all she had, and grown worse. She touches Jesus' clothes from behind in the crowd, is healed at once, and then in fear and trembling tells him the whole truth. Jesus calls her 'Daughter' and tells her to go in peace.

l: healing of the bleeding woman, The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 5
s: On the way to Jairus's house, the woman touches Jesus' clothes, her bleeding dries up immediately, and she feels in her body that she is healed. Jesus perceives that power has gone out from him and asks who touched him, then tells her that her faith has made her well.

l: raising of Jairus's daughter, The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 5
s: After news that the girl is dead, Jesus goes to the house with Peter, James, John, and the parents, puts out the ridiculing mourners, and takes the girl by the hand. She rises and walks immediately, and those present are amazed. Jesus strictly orders that no one should know of it.

l: The Good News According to Mark, The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 6
s: In Chapter 6, Jesus teaches in his own country's synagogue, where people take offense at him and he can heal only a few sick people. He sends the twelve out two by two with authority over unclean spirits, and they preach repentance, cast out demons, and anoint and heal the sick. King Herod, hearing of Jesus, believes John the Baptizer has risen; the text recounts how Herod, at his birthday supper, was pressed by an oath to have John beheaded at the request of Herodias and her daughter. The apostles return, Jesus takes them to a deserted place, and he feeds five thousand men with five loaves and two fish. Jesus then walks on the sea to his straining disciples and calms the wind, and at Gennesaret the people bring the sick to him to touch his garment and be made well.

l: Jesus, The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 6
s: Jesus teaches in the synagogue in his own country, is rejected by those who know his family, and says a prophet is not without honor except in his own country. He sends out the twelve, has compassion on a great multitude and feeds them, walks on the sea to his disciples, and heals the sick at Gennesaret.

l: disciples (Jesus's disciples), The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 6
s: The disciples follow Jesus, and the twelve are sent out in pairs with authority over unclean spirits. After returning to report, they suggest sending the crowd away, distribute the loaves and fish, and gather twelve baskets of pieces. They are terrified when they see Jesus walking on the sea, supposing him a ghost, and the text says they had not understood about the loaves and their hearts were hardened.

l: Herod, The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 6
s: King Herod hears of Jesus and says John the Baptizer, whom he beheaded, has risen from the dead. The text explains that he had arrested John for the sake of Herodias, feared him as a righteous and holy man, and heard him gladly. At his birthday supper he swore to give the young lady whatever she asked and, though exceedingly sorry, ordered John's beheading to honor his oaths and his guests.

l: John the Baptizer, The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 6
s: John had told Herod it was not lawful for him to have his brother's wife, and Herod bound him in prison for that reason. Herod protected him, but he was beheaded in the prison at Herodias's request, and his head was brought on a platter. His disciples took his corpse and laid it in a tomb.

l: Herodias, The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 6
