s: Herodias, formerly the wife of Herod's brother Philip, set herself against John and wanted to kill him but could not while Herod protected him. When her daughter asked what to request, she told her to ask for the head of John the Baptizer, and she received it from her daughter.

l: daughter of Herodias, The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 6
s: She came in and danced, pleasing Herod and his guests, and the king offered her whatever she wanted. After consulting her mother, she asked for John's head on a platter, received it, and gave it to her mother.

l: Herod's birthday banquet, The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 6
s: Herod made a supper on his birthday for his nobles, high officers, and the chief men of Galilee. During it the daughter of Herodias danced, Herod swore to give her whatever she asked up to half his kingdom, and this led to John's beheading.

l: mission of the twelve, The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 6
s: Jesus called the twelve and sent them out two by two with authority over unclean spirits, instructing them to take only a staff, wear sandals, and stay in one house in each place. They were to shake off the dust against places that refused them. They preached repentance, cast out many demons, and anointed and healed many sick people, then gathered to tell Jesus all they had done and taught.

l: multitude, The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 6
s: Many people recognized Jesus and his disciples leaving by boat and ran on foot from all the cities, arriving ahead of them. Jesus had compassion on them as sheep without a shepherd and taught them. They were seated in groups of hundreds and fifties, all ate and were filled, and Jesus then sent them away.

l: feeding of the five thousand, The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 6
s: Late in the day in a deserted place, Jesus told the disciples to give the crowd something to eat. He took five loaves and two fish, looked up to heaven, blessed and broke them, and had the disciples set them before the people. All ate and were filled, twelve baskets of pieces were gathered, and five thousand men had eaten.

l: loaves and fish, The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 6
s: The disciples found five loaves and two fish among the crowd. Jesus blessed and broke the loaves and divided the fish, and the disciples distributed them. Twelve baskets full of broken pieces and fish remained.

l: Jesus walking on the sea, The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 6
s: Jesus sent his disciples ahead by boat to Bethsaida and went up the mountain to pray. About the fourth watch he came to them walking on the sea as they struggled against a contrary wind, and he would have passed by them. They thought him a ghost and cried out, but he told them to cheer up and not be afraid, got into the boat, and the wind ceased.

l: Gennesaret, The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 6
s: After crossing the sea, the boat came to land and moored at Gennesaret. The people recognized Jesus at once and ran around the region bringing the sick on mats to where he was.

l: healing of the sick, The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 6
s: In his own country Jesus laid hands on a few sick people and healed them, and the twelve anointed many sick with oil and healed them. At Gennesaret and in villages, cities, and the country, people laid the sick in marketplaces and begged to touch the fringe of his garment. As many as touched him were made well.

l: The Good News According to Mark, The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 7
s: Pharisees and scribes from Jerusalem fault Jesus' disciples for eating with unwashed hands, breaking the tradition of the elders. Jesus answers by quoting Isaiah, accusing them of hypocrisy, and showing that through the Corban practice they set aside God's commandment to honor father and mother. He then teaches the multitude and, privately, his disciples that what enters a man cannot defile him, but evil things proceeding from the heart do. Jesus goes to the borders of Tyre and Sidon, where a Greek Syrophoenician woman begs him to cast a demon out of her daughter; after her reply about the dogs and the crumbs, he tells her the demon has gone, and she finds the child on the bed. Returning to the sea of Galilee through Decapolis, Jesus heals a deaf man with a speech impediment, and though told to be silent, the people proclaim it and are astonished.

l: Jesus, The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 7
s: Jesus rebukes the Pharisees and scribes as hypocrites, saying they set aside God's commandment for human tradition, and teaches that what comes out of a man defiles him, not what goes in. He goes to Tyre and Sidon, tests and then grants a Syrophoenician woman's request, and heals a deaf man with a speech impediment in the Decapolis region, commanding silence that is not kept.

l: Pharisees, The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 7
s: The Pharisees, with some scribes from Jerusalem, find fault with the disciples for eating with unwashed hands and ask why they don't follow the tradition of the elders. Jesus calls them hypocrites who honor God with their lips while their hearts are far away, and who reject God's commandment to keep their tradition.

l: scribes, The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 7
s: Some scribes who came from Jerusalem gather with the Pharisees and join in questioning Jesus about his disciples' unwashed hands. They are included in Jesus' rebuke as hypocrites who hold to the tradition of men.

l: disciples (Jesus's disciples), The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 7
s: Jesus' disciples are criticized for eating bread with unwashed hands. Later, in a house, they ask him about the parable, and he asks whether they too are without understanding before explaining that food goes into the stomach and makes all foods clean.

l: tradition of the elders, The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 7
s: The tradition of the elders is described as the practice of the Pharisees and all the Jews of washing hands and forearms before eating, bathing after the marketplace, and washing cups, pitchers, bronze vessels, and couches. Jesus calls it a tradition of men that is held tightly while God's commandment is set aside.

l: ritual washing and defilement, The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 7
s: The Pharisees treat eating with unwashed hands as defiling. Jesus teaches that nothing entering a man from outside can defile him, since it goes into the stomach and then the latrine, making all foods clean, and that only what proceeds out of the man defiles him.

l: commandment of God, The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 7
s: Jesus says the Pharisees and scribes set aside God's commandment, citing Moses' words to honor father and mother and that whoever speaks evil of them should be put to death. He says their tradition makes void the word of God.

l: Corban, The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 7
s: Corban is a vow, explained as 'given to God,' by which a man says that whatever profit his father or mother might have received from him is Corban. Jesus says this tradition stops a person from doing anything for his parents and so voids God's word.

l: evil things from within the heart, The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 7
s: Jesus lists what proceeds from within the hearts of men: evil thoughts, adulteries, sexual sins, murders, thefts, covetings, wickedness, deceit, lustful desires, an evil eye, blasphemy, pride, and foolishness. He says all these come from within and defile the man.

l: Syrophoenician woman, The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 7
s: A Greek woman, a Syrophoenician by race, falls at Jesus' feet in a house near Tyre and begs him to cast a demon out of her little daughter. When Jesus says the children should be filled first and bread not thrown to dogs, she answers that even the dogs under the table eat the children's crumbs. For this saying, he tells her to go her way, and she returns home to find her daughter healed.

l: daughter (Syrophoenician woman's daughter), The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 7
s: The Syrophoenician woman's little daughter has an unclean spirit. After Jesus speaks, her mother finds her laid on the bed with the demon gone out.

l: unclean spirit (the demon), The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 7
s: An unclean spirit afflicts the Syrophoenician woman's little daughter. Jesus declares that the demon has gone out of her, and it is found to be gone when the woman reaches home.

l: deaf man with speech impediment, The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 7
s: People bring to Jesus a man who is deaf and has an impediment in his speech, begging Jesus to lay his hand on him. Jesus takes him aside privately, and the man's ears are opened and his tongue released so that he speaks clearly.

l: healing of the deaf man, The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 7
s: Jesus takes the man aside, puts his fingers into his ears, spits and touches his tongue, looks up to heaven, sighs, and says 'Ephphatha,' meaning 'Be opened.' The man is immediately healed. Jesus commands silence, but the more he commands it, the more widely it is proclaimed, and the people are astonished that he does all things well.

l: The Good News According to Mark, The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 8
s: Jesus has compassion on a hungry multitude of about four thousand and feeds them with seven loaves and a few small fish, leaving seven baskets of leftovers. He then crosses to Dalmanutha, where the Pharisees ask for a sign from heaven and he refuses, and in the boat he warns his disciples about the yeast of the Pharisees and Herod, rebuking their misunderstanding by recalling the two feedings. At Bethsaida he heals a blind man in two stages. Near Caesarea Philippi Peter declares Jesus is the Christ, Jesus foretells his suffering, death and resurrection, rebukes Peter for objecting, and calls the multitude and his disciples to deny themselves, take up their cross and follow him.

l: Jesus, The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 8
s: Jesus feeds four thousand with seven loaves and a few fish, refuses the Pharisees a sign, and warns his disciples about the yeast of the Pharisees and Herod. He heals a blind man at Bethsaida, accepts Peter's confession that he is the Christ, foretells his suffering, death and resurrection, rebukes Peter, and teaches the cost of following him.

l: disciples (Jesus's disciples), The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 8
s: The disciples ask how so many could be satisfied with bread in a deserted place, then serve the multitude and gather seven baskets of leftovers. They misunderstand Jesus' warning about yeast, thinking it concerns having no bread, and Jesus asks whether they yet understand, recalling the twelve and seven baskets. They are later asked who people say Jesus is and are taught about his coming suffering, and are commanded to tell no one about him.

l: multitude (four thousand), The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 8
s: A great multitude has stayed with Jesus three days with nothing to eat. About four thousand eat and are filled, and Jesus sends them away. Later Jesus calls a multitude to himself with his disciples and teaches them about denying oneself and taking up the cross.

l: seven loaves, The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 8
s: The disciples report they have seven loaves. Jesus takes them, gives thanks, breaks them, and has the disciples serve the multitude, along with a few small fish he blessed. Seven baskets of broken pieces are left over, and Jesus later recalls this when questioning the disciples.

l: Pharisees, The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 8
s: The Pharisees come out and question Jesus, seeking a sign from heaven and testing him. Jesus sighs deeply and says no sign will be given to this generation, then leaves them. He afterward warns his disciples to beware of their yeast.

l: yeast of the Pharisees and Herod, The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 8
s: Jesus warns his disciples to take heed and beware of the yeast of the Pharisees and the yeast of Herod. The disciples wrongly think he speaks of having no bread, and Jesus rebukes their lack of perception and understanding.

l: blind man, The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 8
s: People bring a blind man to Jesus at Bethsaida and beg him to touch him. Jesus leads him out of the village, spits on his eyes and lays hands on him, and the man first sees people like walking trees. After a second laying on of hands he sees everyone clearly, and Jesus sends him home, telling him not to enter the village or tell anyone there.

l: Peter, The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 8
s: Peter answers Jesus' question about who the disciples say he is by saying, "You are the Christ." When Jesus openly teaches that he must suffer and be killed, Peter takes him aside and begins to rebuke him. Jesus rebukes Peter in turn, saying, "Get behind me, Satan!" because Peter has in mind the things of men, not of God.

l: Christ, The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 8
s: Peter identifies Jesus as the Christ at Caesarea Philippi after the disciples report what others say about him: John the Baptizer, Elijah, or one of the prophets. Jesus commands the disciples to tell no one about him.

l: Jesus's death and resurrection (predicted), The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 8
s: Jesus begins to teach that the Son of Man must suffer many things, be rejected by the elders, chief priests and scribes, be killed, and after three days rise again. He speaks of this openly, and Peter's rebuke of it is itself rebuked by Jesus.

l: discipleship and taking up the cross, The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 8
s: Jesus tells the multitude and his disciples that whoever wants to come after him must deny himself, take up his cross, and follow him. He says whoever tries to save his life will lose it, while whoever loses it for his sake and the Good News will save it, and he warns that those ashamed of him and his words will be met with the Son of Man's shame when he comes in glory.

l: The Good News According to Mark, The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 9
s: In Mark 9, Jesus takes Peter, James, and John up a high mountain, where he is changed in appearance, Elijah and Moses appear, and a voice from a cloud calls him the beloved Son. Coming down, he tells them to keep silent until the Son of Man has risen, and he explains that Elijah has already come. Jesus then casts a mute spirit out of a boy whom his disciples could not help, after the boy's father cries out, "I believe. Help my unbelief!" Passing through Galilee, Jesus twice foretells his death and resurrection, but the disciples do not understand. They argue about who is greatest, and Jesus teaches them about being last and servant of all, receiving little children, not forbidding others who act in his name, and avoiding causes of stumbling.

l: Jesus, The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 9
s: Jesus is transfigured before Peter, James, and John, is declared the beloved Son by a voice from a cloud, and heals a boy by rebuking a mute and deaf spirit. He predicts his death and rising on the third day, and teaches the twelve that the first must be last and servant of all, that those not against them are for them, and that stumbling blocks must be removed.

l: Peter, The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 9
s: Peter goes up the mountain with Jesus, James, and John and, afraid and not knowing what to say, proposes making three tents for Jesus, Moses, and Elijah. He is one of those who keep the command to tell no one what they saw until the Son of Man has risen.

l: Elijah, The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 9
s: Elijah appears with Moses and talks with Jesus on the mountain. Jesus tells the disciples that Elijah indeed comes first and restores all things, and that Elijah has already come and people did to him whatever they wanted, as it is written.

l: God, The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 9
s: God is the one whose Kingdom will come with power, as Jesus says some standing there will see before tasting death. A voice from the cloud identifies Jesus as "my beloved Son" and tells the three to listen to him. Jesus says that receiving him means receiving the one who sent him.

l: disciples (Jesus's disciples), The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 9
s: The disciples fail to cast the spirit out of the boy, and Jesus tells them privately that this kind comes out only by prayer and fasting. They do not understand Jesus's prediction of his death and are afraid to ask, and they argue on the way about who is greatest. John reports they forbade an outsider casting out demons in Jesus's name, and Jesus tells them not to forbid him.

l: father (father of the boy), The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 9
s: The father brings his son to Jesus and describes the spirit's long attacks, which have thrown the boy into fire and water since childhood. When Jesus says all things are possible to him who believes, he cries out with tears, "I believe. Help my unbelief!"

l: boy (the possessed son), The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 9
s: The boy is seized by a mute spirit that throws him down, makes him foam, grind his teeth, and become rigid. After Jesus commands the spirit out, the boy lies like one dead, and Jesus takes his hand and raises him up, and he arises.

l: mute spirit (the boy's spirit), The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 9
s: The mute spirit has afflicted the boy since childhood and convulses him when he is brought to Jesus. Jesus rebukes it as a mute and deaf spirit and commands it to come out and never enter him again, and it leaves after crying out and convulsing him greatly.

l: Transfiguration, The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 9
s: Six days after the preceding teaching, Jesus is changed into another form on a high mountain before Peter, James, and John, his clothing becoming glistening, exceedingly white. Elijah and Moses appear and talk with him, and a voice from a cloud calls him the beloved Son. Afterward Jesus commands the three to tell no one until the Son of Man has risen.

l: Jesus's death and resurrection (predicted), The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 9
s: Jesus tells the three to keep silent about the vision until the Son of Man has risen from the dead, and they wonder what rising from the dead means. Later, while passing through Galilee, he says the Son of Man will be handed over to men, killed, and rise on the third day, but the disciples do not understand.

l: dispute over who was greatest, The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 9
s: On the way to Capernaum the disciples dispute among themselves about who is the greatest, and they are silent when Jesus asks about it in the house. Jesus sits down, calls the twelve, and says whoever wants to be first must be last of all and servant of all, then sets a little child among them as an example.

l: The Good News According to Mark, The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 10
s: In Mark 10, Jesus travels into Judea and beyond the Jordan, where Pharisees test him about divorce and he answers by pointing to God's creation of male and female and the union of husband and wife. He receives little children over the disciples' objection, then tells a man with great possessions who asks about eternal life to sell everything and follow him, and the man goes away sorrowful. Jesus teaches his disciples about the difficulty of riches entering God's Kingdom and for the third time predicts his condemnation, death, and rising on the way to Jerusalem. James and John ask for seats at his right and left, which prompts Jesus to teach that greatness means serving. At Jericho he restores the sight of the blind beggar Bartimaeus, who then follows him.

l: Jesus, The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 10
s: Jesus teaches multitudes, answers the Pharisees on divorce, welcomes little children, and tells a man with great possessions to sell all and follow him. He predicts his death and rising, teaches that the Son of Man came to serve and give his life as a ransom for many, and heals Bartimaeus at Jericho.

l: Pharisees, The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 10
s: The Pharisees come to Jesus to test him, asking whether it is lawful for a man to divorce his wife. Jesus turns them to what Moses commanded and explains that Moses allowed it because of their hardness of heart.

l: disciples (Jesus's disciples), The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 10
s: The disciples ask Jesus again about divorce, rebuke those bringing children, and are amazed at his teaching on riches. Peter says they have left all to follow him, and the ten become indignant at James and John. Jesus takes the twelve aside to tell them what will happen to him in Jerusalem.

l: God, The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 10
s: God made them male and female from the beginning of creation and joins a husband and wife together. Jesus says that no one is good except God alone and that all things are possible with God, so salvation, impossible for men, is possible with him.

l: divorce, The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 10
s: Jesus says Moses allowed a certificate of divorce because of hardness of heart, but that from creation the two become one flesh, and what God has joined let no man separate. He adds that whoever divorces and marries another commits adultery, whether man or woman.

l: little children (brought to Jesus), The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 10
s: Little children are brought to Jesus so that he may touch them, and the disciples rebuke those bringing them. Jesus is indignant, says God's Kingdom belongs to such as these, then takes them in his arms and blesses them.

l: God's Kingdom, The Good News According to Mark, Chapter 10
s: Jesus says it belongs to such as little children and that whoever does not receive it like a little child will not enter it. He also says it is hard for those who have or trust in riches to enter, easier for a camel to pass through a needle's eye.
